title: Ship on Friday with a known bug (the owner interrupts and questions)
motion: The team ships the v2 payments API this Friday as planned, with the known duplicate-charge bug unfixed, and fixes it in the following release.
context: Background (fictional, for this exercise): v2 of the payments API is due to ship this Friday. Testing found a bug: when a client retries a charge request after a network timeout, about 1 in 2000 charges is applied twice. The fix is understood but needs about two weeks including a safe migration. Shipping on time satisfies a signed launch commitment to the largest customer; each week of delay costs the company a contractual penalty. Nothing here is real-world knowledge: rely only on your own background and notes, and use your own judgment.

agents.name: Dana
agents.role: backend engineer who wrote the charge code
agents.persona: You wrote the retry path where the bug lives and know it best.
desk: The duplicate only happens when the client retries after a timeout and the first request had actually succeeded.
Our existing refund tool reverses a duplicate in about 5 minutes of manual work per case; no customer data is exposed.
At the expected volume of 40,000 charges a week, 1 in 2000 means about 20 duplicates a week.

agents.name: Ravi
agents.role: engineer on call for customer-facing incidents
agents.persona: You carry the pager and talk to affected customers when something goes wrong.
desk: The last billing incident, a single double charge, produced 14 support tickets and two customers asking to cancel.
Customers see a double charge as a trust problem even when refunded within the hour.
I have no data on whether the largest customer would accept a short delay.

agents.name: Mei
agents.role: engineer who leads the launch work
agents.persona: You coordinate the launch with the largest customer's team.
desk: The launch commitment is in the contract; the penalty is 20 thousand dollars per week of delay.
The largest customer's own go-live is Monday and it will use the new API from day one.
I have not asked the customer whether a two-week delay is acceptable.

afterRound1.message: Owner here. Before round 2: I am worried about the customer more than the penalty. Please keep that in mind.

questions.text: Ravi, how many customers could a double charge realistically reach in the first month, and what would you tell them?

afterRound1.command: Thanks, that is all for now; carry on.

duringVote.message: Owner here, pausing the vote. I will ask a couple of things before anyone finalizes.

questions.text: Dana, could the retry path be made safe with a small interim guard, such as an idempotency key, in under two days? Be honest if you do not know.
Mei, what exactly would you need from the customer to move Friday?

duringVote.command: Done with questions. Carry on with the vote.
